2.plain: A server speed test that crashed whenever bots played now runs.

3.plain: The 50-player server stress test connects every player properly again.

13.plain: Shot and sight checks skip walls they can't touch, so the server does less work.

14.plain: Player movement checks skip walls they can't touch, so the server does less work.

16.plain: Two game tests now run on Windows PCs too.

17.plain: The full test suite now runs on Windows PCs.

19.plain: Bot sight lines skip map squares they never pass through. With #13 and #14, the server's work per tick fell by about a third.

21.plain: Water reflections cost about a quarter less to draw, with no visible change.

23.plain: The game prepares its effects before you drop in, so the first frame of a match is about 6 times quicker.

25.plain: Slow computers no longer fail to load because of a cosmetic far-tree effect.

28.plain: The game's start-up script runs about a second faster on a Windows PC.

32.plain: Sharing a link to the game now shows a proper preview card.

35.plain: The game skips painting a character model it isn't going to use.

36.plain: Two big locations build in small steps, so the match warm-up hitches less.

37.plain: The game keeps loading even if the browser window is covered or hidden.

41.plain: The island map is painted in the background, so the page doesn't freeze while it loads.

46.plain: Picking up items stopped creating throwaway memory: 55% less memory churn per tick.

47.plain: Loot is placed using each match's own cover walls.

59.plain: Rocket and bomb messages are always read in full, so the message after them isn't misread.

60.plain: Locations that stream in during warm-up cause smaller hitches: the worst one went from 641 ms to 410 ms.

69.plain: Bots stopped creating throwaway memory every tick.

83.plain: Testers can save debug settings in the browser.

85.plain: The game learns how long each computer takes to finish loading, so it can plan a faster title screen.

87.plain: Keeps the first download small by loading that new timing code only when it's needed.

88.plain: The game stops preparing graphics it throws away, so the title shows up 4 seconds sooner on a Windows PC.

perf.name: Title screen ready, v0.2.0 vs kong-v0.6.1 (Windows Chrome)
perf.plain: Compared with the version we started from, the title screen shows up about 12 seconds sooner on a first visit.
perf.metric: readyMs, cold, median. v0.2.0: 3 loads [31.6-33.1] (RAY-94). kong-v0.6.1: 5 loads [17.7-22.3], interleaved with v0.6.0, tools/performance/load-profile.mts. Different days and tool versions, so indicative
perf.source: v0.2.0: RAY-94 precise re-run (f000fd1). kong-v0.6.1: project drive handoffs/release-kong-v0.6.1-d3d11/load-table.md (cold readyMs 19233, ee43574)

perf.name: Whole-browser memory at the title screen, v0.2.0 vs main (Windows)
perf.plain: The browser holds about 1.9 GB less at the title screen than it did on v0.2.0. Part of that is the lower default quality setting.
perf.metric: whole browser (browser, renderer and GPU processes), median of 3 runs a side, memory.mts v3, kong-v0.2.0 boots at ultra quality and main at high, so not a same-quality test

perf.name: Whole-browser memory 30 s into a match, v0.2.0 vs main (Windows)
perf.plain: The browser holds about 2.1 GB less in a match than it did on v0.2.0. Part of that is the lower default quality setting.
perf.metric: whole browser (browser, renderer and GPU processes), median of 3 runs a side, memory.mts v3, kong-v0.2.0 boots at ultra quality and main at high, so not a same-quality test

perf.name: 3D shapes loaded at the title screen
perf.plain: About 210 more 3D shapes are loaded when the title appears than in v0.2.0, and about 420 more 30 seconds into a match.
perf.metric: three.js renderer.info geometries at __kr.ready, median of 3, [580-663] to [616-855]. Plane 2819 to 3045, 30 s into the match 3047 to 3464
perf.source: RAY-94 precise re-run (--enable-precise-memory-info, #90): v0.2.0 f000fd1 vs main 290a32b, 3 cold runs a side, indicative

perf.name: Title screen ready, Windows Chrome (first visit)
perf.plain: The title screen now shows up 4 seconds sooner on a first visit, because the game stops preparing graphics it throws away.
perf.metric: __kr.readyAt, cold, median of 5 interleaved per side, [28.4-31.6] to [24.3-27.5]; settle warm-up 3908 ms to 501 ms; first match frame unchanged within noise. Metal is unmeasured

perf.name: Server work per tick
perf.plain: The server does a third less work to run each moment of a match, so one machine can host more games.
perf.metric: Real-play host tick p50 on a seeded match; results are replay-identical
perf.source: reports/KONG-20.md (Stack status) and NOTES.md 2026-11-04; fork PRs #13, #14, #19

perf.name: Memory churn per tick
perf.plain: The game creates far less throwaway memory, so the computer pauses less often to clean up.
perf.metric: allocBytesPerTick on real-play; garbage collections 183 to 82, GC time 178 ms to 87 ms

perf.name: First frame of a match (processor)
perf.plain: The first moment after you drop in no longer freezes: it's about 6 times quicker.
perf.metric: First match frame, CPU step, median [851-1461] to [146-160]

perf.name: First frame of a match (graphics card)
perf.plain: The graphics card's share of that first frame went from almost half a second to a blink.
perf.metric: First match frame, GPU time, median [442-1051] to [23-47]

perf.name: Worst hitch during match warm-up
perf.plain: The biggest stutter while the island streams in is a third shorter.
perf.metric: Worst frame interval in the first 15 s, median [525-819] to [402-640]

perf.name: Slowest 1% of warm-up frames

perf.metric: Frame interval p99 in the first 15 s

perf.metric: phase.mainScriptMs median 5375 (4533-6134) to about 2.9 s (2794-3033)

phases.name: Safety checks for every change
phases.plain: Automatic tests that prove the game still works, on Mac, Windows and in the cloud.
issues: Pass/fail thresholds for the bot match and lag lab
Verification skill for Mac, Windows and cloud
Cloud boot without a graphics card
Loading can't fail on a cosmetic effect
Boot check without a graphics card
Tests for bug reports and voice
Slow first 15 s of a match

phases.name: Ready for many contributors
phases.plain: Turning every project rule into an automatic check so lots of changes can land safely at once.
issues: Match checks, golden results and replays
Formal models of vehicle seats and match phases
Line endings, cloud boot check, link previews

phases.name: Performance plan
phases.plain: Measure first, then make the game and server faster, keeping only changes the numbers prove.
issues: Loot search index (tried; the numbers said no)
Performance plan document brought up to date

phases.name: Faster loading
phases.plain: Cutting the time from opening the page to the title screen.
issues: Warm only the shaders we need
Defer far loot detail until after the title

phases.name: Releases
phases.plain: Numbered releases with a test channel (next) and a public channel (stable), plus fast rollback.
issues: Release tool, labels and the first release

asks.what: Pick where the stable release is hosted.

inProgress.name: Cut memory so 16 GB Macs play without swapping
inProgress.estimate: Chrome uses about 9.9 GB for the whole browser. Safari survived a full match in the latest test with a peak of 6.9 to 7.3 GB, but it was killed at 8.4 to 8.8 GB in earlier runs, so the margin is thin (tracked as RAY-104 to RAY-106)

releaseTrain.plain: A new release can go out four times a day, at 10 AM, 1 PM, 4 PM and 7 PM Pacific, whenever there are changes waiting.

summary.plain: Since v0.2.0, the project has made the game faster to load, smoother to start and cheaper to run, with every change measured before and after.
